hosts.question: What can the HOST tell us about agents running inside it, without per-harness work? Cover cmux (socket RPC, hooks, feed, notifications), Ghostty, iTerm2, Warp, WezTerm, kitty, tmux, and the terminal conventions OSC 9;4 (progress), OSC 133 (prompt and command marks), OSC 9 and 777 (notifications).

studies.question: Other tools already detect which coding agents are running and whether each is working, idle or blocked. Study how they do it, from their source code where it is public: Herdr (read its agent detection and state logic closely: what it matches on, how it decides working versus idle versus blocked, whether it reads the screen, hooks, process state or files), cmux, Agent Sessions (jazzyalex/agent-sessions), CASS (Dicklesworthstone/coding_agent_session_search), Claude Squad, Conductor, Emdash, vibe-kanban, and any other you find. For each: the mechanism, the list of harnesses it supports, and what it gets right that our registry does not. Then DIFF: list every harness any of them supports that has no file in registry/agents/ and is not in registry/harnesses.json, with the source that names it. That list is the main deliverable.
studies.local_hint: cmux is installed on this Mac; its shell integration and wrapper scripts are under /Applications/cmux.app/Contents/Resources. Herdr is not installed; read its repository.

studies.question: registry/evidence/hosts.md studied cmux, Ghostty, iTerm2, Warp, WezTerm, kitty and tmux. Extend it to the hosts it left out: Herdr (does it expose a socket, CLI or file another program can read for agent state, and does that need setup), Terminal.app (AppleScript: busy, processes, tty, title), Zellij, Alacritty, and the integrated terminals of VS Code, Cursor and JetBrains IDEs. Answer for each: what it knows about a running agent, how another same-user process can ask it, whether that needs consent or configuration, and how reliable it is. Do not repeat what hosts.md already establishes; cite it.
studies.local_hint: Terminal.app is present on every Mac; you may read its scripting dictionary with `sdef /System/Applications/Utilities/Terminal.app` but do not send it Apple events that open windows or run commands.
